title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DESMOND'S TURKEY
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Desmond Whitaker, a hotel night auditor in Salt Lake City, Utah.
Desmond counts money at three in the morning and eats from a vending machine.
He had never cooked more than toast. Then his mom twisted her ankle line dancing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BASTER
segments.quote: It's kind of fun to do the impossible.
segments.author: Walt Disney
lines: For forty years, his mom Bernice cooked Thanksgiving for twenty-two relatives.
Now she handed Desmond the turkey baster.
He said, Mom, that's impossible. She smiled and quoted Walt Disney:
It's kind of fun to do the impossible.
Desmond held the baster like a microphone. Then he said yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SMOKE ALARM
segments.author: Louisa May Alcott
lines: Two weeks early, he roasted a practice turkey.
The smoke alarm sang. The neighbors came out in their robes.
His sister Tanya laughed and quoted Louisa May Alcott:
Housekeeping ain't no joke.
So Desmond stopped joking. He bought a meat thermometer and wrote every step down.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: ONE OVEN
segments.quote: Problems are only opportunities in work clothes.
segments.author: Henry J. Kaiser
lines: Then he counted. Eleven dishes. One oven.
His boss at the hotel, Gus, quoted the shipbuilder Henry J. Kaiser:
Problems are only opportunities in work clothes.
So Desmond put the family to work. Everybody brings one dish.
Uncle Ray got the rolls. Nobody can burn rolls. Probably.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE DEAD OVEN
segments.quote: No one is so brave that he is not disturbed by something unexpected.
segments.author: Julius Caesar
lines: Thanksgiving morning, the oven died. The turkey was still raw.
Desmond froze. His mom quoted Julius Caesar, the old Roman general:
No one is so brave that he is not disturbed by something unexpected.
Breathe, she said. Then think.
Desmond called Gus. The turkey roasted in the hotel kitchen and rode home on a room service cart.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LUMPY POTATOES
segments.quote: Have patience with all things, but chiefly have patience with yourself.
segments.author: Saint Francis de Sales
lines: Back home, the mashed potatoes came out lumpy.
Desmond grumbled at himself. Tanya quoted the old French writer Francis de Sales:
Have patience with all things, but chiefly have patience with yourself.
So Desmond laughed, called the lumps a family secret, and carried the bowl out.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG TABLE
segments.quote: Small cheer and great welcome makes a merry feast.
segments.author: William Shakespeare
lines: Twenty-two people squeezed around two tables and a ping-pong table.
Not every dish was perfect. Everybody went back for seconds anyway.
Bernice raised her glass and quoted Shakespeare:
Small cheer and great welcome makes a merry feast.
Then she handed Desmond the baster for good. Same time next year, she said.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Take it seriously. Share the work. Breathe. Go easy on yourself. Open the door.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes. Take it seriously. Share the work. Breathe. Go easy on yourself. Open the door wide.
I cooked a turkey once. The fire department still sends me a card every November.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
